Women empowerment  
t*481. SHRI JANESHWAR MISHRA: Will the Minister of WOMEN AND CHILD 
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:  
(a)  whether it is a fact that a report prepared recentl y by London School of Oriental & 
African Studies, has indicated about the negligence towards and poor condition of women; 
(b)  if so, whether the so called women empowerment is proving to be deceptive, with half 
of the population of the country; 
tOriginal notice of the question was received in Hindi.  

4   Oral Answers  [RAJYA SABHA]  to Questions  
(c)  if so, whether Government is formulating any effective scheme to enable women to 
get rid of these basic problems; and 
(d)  if so, the details thereof? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINISTRY OF WOMEN AND CHILD 
DEVELOPMENT (SHRIMATI RENUKA CHOWDHURY): (a) to (d) A Statement is laid on 
the Table of the House.  
Statement  
(a) Government is not aware of any such report of the London School of Oriental & 
African Studies.  
(b)to(d)Do not arise.

SHRIMATI RENUKA CHOWDHURY: Mr. Chairman, Sir, I want to thank the hon. Member for giving me this 
compliment in the beginning. But I also want to point out that the question is very, very specific and it 
refers to a report prepared by the London School of Oriental and African Studies, which has indicated 
about the negligence towards poor conditions of women. The reply that we have drafted directly addresses 
that very issue that we are not aware of this particular study. We have on record an e-mail, which I can forward 
to the hon. Member later, in which the school has said that they are not aware of what these  

Oral Answers  [28 APRIL, 2008]  to Questions   5 
studies are and from where these reports have been culled and derived. Hence my inability 
and my limitations. I cannot misguide the House by quoting from a report about which I do 
not know anything. Sir, Shri Janeshwar Mishra is a senior and seasoned politician for whom 
we have great respect. We are aware of the outstanding works that he has done in various 
activities. There is no doubt about the commitment of this Government or my personal 
commitment towards the issue of women and child development. We have a more holistic 
approach where we dovetail and take interventions, along with other Ministries, to ensure 
that there is enabling and empowered atomosphere in the country for women. We do vote 
for political, social and economic development as well as gender justice, gender budgeting 
and advocacy which is done at various levels. There are exhaustive schemes which speak 
about this. There are exhaustive schemes which speak about this. And we are approaching 
the Eleventh Plan in a pro-active way so that we plug, if there are any in the first-place, the 
loopholes, to ensure that the safety net that we give to woman and child development and 
empowerment will continue to rise dramatically, and the infant mortality, maternal mortality, 
feeding of child, nutrition, access to food security, education, immunisation, domestic 
violence, all these, are taken care of. Now, despite the fact that it is State Governments, 
which are supposed to be having the authority to ensure implementation of this, I dont 
think I am known to be polite or patient and wait for States to deliver. We have been pro-
active in various States to ensure that studies and comparatives, as well as, interventions 
are taken to protect these women. For example, the Domestic Violence Act, which we brought 
in last year,...  
MR. CHAIRMAN: Let him put his second supplementary. 
SHRI MATI RENUKACHOWDHURY: He has put a specific supplementary, and hence 
I am answering it. I would like to mention that this Act was reviewed within a period of 
one year; perhaps, the first time ever that the Government of India had taken this on a pro-
active manner, and we have shown dramatic results in that.

(b)  if so, whether there is a demand to from a Third Schedule for OBCs and Vimukti Jati 
and Nomadic Tribes (VJNT); 
(c)  if so, whether Government has taken/proposes to take steps in view of the said 
demand; and 
(d)  if so, the details thereof? 
THE MINISTER OF SOCIAL JUSTICE AND EMPOWERMENT (SHRIMATI MEIRA 
KUMAR): (a) to (d) A Statement is laid on the Table of the House.  
Statement  
(a) to (d) The Central Government has already been notifying lists of "backward classes" 
other than those of Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes, from time to time.  
Government has constituted a National Commission for Denotified, Nomadic and Semi-
Nomadic Tribes with the following terms of reference:  
(i) To specify the economic interventions required for raising the living standards of 
Denotified, Nomadic and Semi-Nomadic Tribes' by asset creation and self-
employment opportunities;  
(ii) To recommend measures to utilize the existing channeling agencies set up for the 
economic development of SC/STs and OBCs for extendi ng an economic 
development package to these groups, keeping in view their specific requirements;  
(iii) To identify programmes required for their education, development and health; and  
(iv) To make any other connected or incidental recommendation, that the commission 
deems necessary.

SHRIMATI MEIRA KUMAR: Sir, I am very happy that fin ally a question has been 
asked about the written question and you have confi ned yourself to this. About the DNT, 
Denotified Tribe, Nomadic and Semi-Nomadic Tribes, some of them are listed in the SC list, 
some are listed in the ST list and some are listed in the OBC list and depending upon which 
list they are included in, they enjoy those facilities.  
If they are listed in the S.C. List, they will get benefits under the S.C. List.  
The hon. Member is talking about Maharashtra. Let m e tell you what the position in 
Maharashtra is. Sir, in Maharashtra, 14 De-notified  Tribes are listed in the OBC List. So, 
they are getting the same facilities that are available to the SCs and the OBCs.  
About hon. Member's specific point that they are no t getting education and hostel 
facilities, I request the hon. Member to write to me and I will be very happy to attend to it.  
DR. K. KESHAVARAO: Sir, my supplementary is pertain ing to Part (a) of the main 
question. I would like to know from the hon. Minist er whether there is any proposal to 
include Backward Classes listed in the State List i n the Central OBC List. The States are 
doing this. But, the Centre is not doing this. The Centre is doing only through the Mandal 
Commission . Every State is including the OBCs into  its List through a Commission. The 
same thing is not being done by the Centre. For example, now, in Andhra Pradesh, there are 
111 BCs in the List which went up from 92. So, will the Government think of a comprehensive 
List? That means, what is listed in the Central Lis t should be accepted by the States and 
what is listed in the State List should be accepted  by the Centre.  
SHRIMATI MEIRA KUMAR: Sir, this matter was settled long ago, considering the 
social complexities of our very large country and different social systems and stratification 
prevailing in different States, there are two Lists. The List which was made by the Mandal 
Commission was the basis for the Central List, thos e OBC classes and castes of State list 
which were common to the Central List were included  in the Central List. So, this is the 
Mandal List. This List is applicable so far as the Central Government posts are concerned. 
But, there has to be a State List, because there ar e so many OBCs in the States which are, 
actually, not common throughout the country. They a re State-specific. So, the provisions 
of reservation are provided to them in the State.

Implementation of Rural Electrification Scheme  
* 483. SHRI HARISH RAWAT:  
SHRIMATI SHOBHANA BHARTIA: Will 
the Minister of POWER be pleased to state:  
(a)  whether the Central Government has recently asked the State Governments to provide 
necessary support to expedite implementation of the Rural Electrification Scheme; 
(b)  if so, the details thereof; 
(c)  whether some State Governments are not implementing  the Scheme in an effective 
way, as a result of which people in rural areas are facing problems; and 
(d)  if so, the steps contemplated by Government to ensure proper implementation of the 
Scheme across the country? 
THE MINISTER OF POWER (SHRI SUSHIL KUMAR SHINDE): (a) to (d) A Statement 
is laid on the Table of the House.  
Statement  
(a) and (b) Yes, Sir. Execution of Rural Electrification works including village electrification 
and release of rural household connections under RG GVY is the responsibility of state 
governments and the concerned state power utilities. Rural Electrification Corporation Ltd. 
(REC) as a nodal agency for RGGVY facilitates flow of funds from Ministry of Power to 
implementing agenices/states, in addition to processing of detailed Project Reports received 
from state governments, monitoring of RGGVY program , and reporting progress to the 
Monitoring Committee on RGGVY. Ministry of Power as also REC have been impressing 
upon the State governments for according priority to implementation of the scheme besides 
extending support and taking suitable action for ex peditious implementation of rural 
electrification works under RGGVY projects within s tipulated timelines for completion of 
projects.  
(c)  Some states are taking more time than the committed  schedule for implementing 
RGGVY works. 
(d)  Ministry of Power also proposes to request State Governments to set up State Level 
Steering Committee under the charimanship of State Chief Secretary comprising Secretaries

of Power, Rural Development, Home, Revenue, Forests and Environment and other related 
departments to resolve implementation issues requiring interdepartmental coordination. This 
Committee will also ensure that there is no delay in issuance of safety clearance prior to taking 
over of completed RGGVY assets by state utilities.  
The following steps have been taken for expeditious and qualitative implementation of the 
scheme.  
Release of funds has been linked with achievement o f milestones reflecting physical 
progress and quality checks as prescribed under Thr ee Tier Quality Monitoring 
Mechanism.  
The Monitoring Committee has already approved 316 projects for execution during 11th 
Plan period, in addition to 235 projects sanctioned for implementation during 10th Plan.  
States have been asked to submit Rural Electrification (RE) Plans incorporating required 
strengthening of sub-transmission system and ensuring at least 6-8 hours electricity to 
electrified villages.  
States have also been asked to make provision for s ubsidies to BPL consumers in their 
budgets.  
States have been asked to coordinate material supplies including supply of poles, cables, 
transformers and sub-station equipment for time-bound implementation of the scheme. A 
National Workshop on the subject was organized by Ministry of Power on 10.04.2008.  
States have been asked to take advance action to ensure that projects are awarded within 3 
months of sanction for facilitating compression of time schedule for implementation of 
projects.  
To ensure qualitative execution of RE works, a three tier quality control mechanism has been 
enforced under RGGVY. A Quality Control manual prepared by REC has been issued to the 
States.  
For effective and expeditious implementation of RGGVY, besides constant follow up periodic 
review meetings are being held by Ministry of Power and REC with the concerned state 
governments implementing agencies and CPSUs.

SHRIMATI SHOBHANA BHARTIA: Sir, one of the major impediments for 
rural , electrification arises in the area of distribution. Sir, to encourage distribution reforms, 
the accelerated Power Development and Reforms Programme was launched with a mandate 
for lowering the transmission and distribution losses from  estimated 45 per cent in 2002 to 
almost 15 per cent by 2007. Sir, the mandate was also to restore the financial health of the 
State Electricity Boards. However, the performance of this Programme has fallen short of the 
promise. The investment in the distribution sector remains very low; and the overall 
transmission and distribution losses remain extremely high. Under such a situation, how 
will the Rural Electrification Scheme actually benefit the consumer? Does the Minister have 
any concrete plans to ensure that the APDRP programme, which has fallen short, can get 
revitalised?  

Oral Answers                                 [28 APRIL, 2008]                             to Questions   19  
SHRI SUSHIL KUMAR SHINDE: Sir, it is a fact that the country was facing these losses, 
particularly, transmission losses and theft losses up to 46 per cent 2-3 years back. But, I am 
happy to mention here that now it has been reduced to 32 per cent. Care has been taken to 
look after this. An hon. Member has said that the project, which we started in the tenth Plan, 
has resulted in increasing the PLF. In some of the cases, the PLF was very low. It was at 
40 per cent. Now, it has increased to 80 per cent now. It has been increasing and, thereby, the 
APDRP Scheme has been accepted in the Eleventh Plan  also. The Scheme is under 
consideration. The hon. member is absolutely correct that because of this, we have given a 
plan to the States. Under the Rajiv Gandhi Gramin Vidyutikaran Scheme, if they want to have 
it in a particular village or State, the State must give 6 to 8 hours undisturbed electricity to 
those places, then, only this Scheme will be extend ed to those States. These types of 
restrictions have been maintained.  
As far as distribution is concerned, many private companies and private called Franchired 
are coming forward. In Maharashtra, it has happened. In West Bengal, it has happened. In 
Andhra Pradesh, it has happened. It has been found that from 44 per cent, the losses have 
come down to 20 per cent in the franchise system.

DR. T. SUBBARAMI REDDY: I am very happy that the hon. Minister has given a very

approved 316 projects for execution during the Eleventh Five Year Plan period, and, in

at present?

Plan under rural electrification scheme and how many villages are being electrified as a

SHRI SUSHIL KUMAR SHINDE: Sir, the hon. Member has put a lot of questions, but I 
have to reply. I will try to reply to them. But before replying to that, I would like to reply to 
the last point of hon. Member, Mabelji's supplementary. Miss Mabel Rebello had said that 
I have not replied to point related to three-phase. Sir, it is up to the State, but under 
Rajiv Gandhi Grameen Vidyutikaran Yojana itself it has been provided that if. Khadi or 
Gramodyog units are there or there is small irrigation purpose, this electricity can be provided.

electrification of unelectrified villages is concerned, as on 31.3.2008, the number is 47,826 
villages and the figure for intensive electrification of electrified villages is"40,838 villages.

connection, including BPL, is 27.72 lakhs in this country. As far as the Tenth Plan and

years of Tenth Plan, i.e., 2005-06 and 2006-07, work on 38,525 villages have been completed 
and in the Eleventh Plan, work on 9301 villages have been completed. Under the intensive 
electrification, in the Tenth Plan, 11,877 villages have been covered and in the Eleventh 
Plan, 28,961 villages have been covered. The cost of the subsidy released during the Tenth 
Plan was Rs. 4,948 crores and in the Eleventh Plan, this year, as we got the money, we have 
released Rs. 3913.45 crores. Sir, since a lengthy question was asked, a lengthy answer is 
given.

Purchase of additional power during peak hours  
t*484.    DR. MURLI MANOHAR JOSHI:  
SHRI  RAM JETHMALANI: Will the 
Minister of POWER be pleased to state:  
(a)  whether it is a fact that additional power during the peak hours is being purchased by 
various States of the country at the rate of seven rupees per unit; 
(b)  if not, the facts in that regard; 
(c)  whether it is also a fact that this power is generally sold at the rate of Rs. 2.50 to 
Rs. 3.50 per unit; 
(d)  if not, the facts in that regard; 
(e)  whether the average cost of power generation in the country is less than its sale 
price; and 
(f)  if so, what is the average cost of power generation? 
THE MINISTER OF POWER (SHRI SUSHIL KUMAR SHINDE): (a) and (b) According to  
the information submitted by trading licensees to the Central Electricity Regulatory  
Commission (CERC) in some cases electricity has been sold in short term trading at the rate  
of Rupees seven per unit. However, the weighted average sale price in short-term trading  
*  during April-December, 2007 was Rs. 4.07 per unit.  
(c) and (d) The energy being purchased in short-term trading is only 2 to 3% of the total 
energy availability and is sold by_the concerned distribution licensee to Consumer after 
pooling with the bulk of the energy purchased by them under the long-term contract. The 
tariff for sale of energy (pooled) by the distribution licensees is determined by the appropriate 
State Electricity Regulatory Commission in terms of Section 62 of Electricity Act, 2003.  
The average all India rates realized for the financial year 2005-06 is Rs. 2.93 per unit.  
(e) and (f) The average cost of generation for thermal, hydro and nuclear power for the 
year 2005-06 is Rs. 1.67 per unit.

IIIT and IIITA in Gujarat  
* 485 . SHRI VIJAYKUMAR RUPANI: Will the Minister of HUMAN RESOURCE 
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:  
(a)  whether the Planning Commission has recommended the setting up of the Indian 
Institute of Information Technology (HIT) and the Indian Institute of Information Technology 
Academy (IIITA) m Gujarat; 
(b)  if so, by when these institutes would be established; and 
(c)  what would be the contribution of the State and the Central Government for these 
institutes? 
THE MINISTER OF HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT (SHRI ARJUN SINGH): 
(a) to (c) The Planning Commission has not made any specific recommendation in regard to 
the location of any Indian Institute of Information Technology (HIT) or an HIT Academy in 
any particular State or in Gujarat. However, a proposal to set up new Indian Institutes of 
Information Technology (IIITs) under Public Private Partnership (PPP) mode is under 
consideration of the Government. The details in this regard are being worked out.  
Policy for minimum use of renewable energy  
*486. SHRI  T.T.V DHTNAKARAN: Will the Minister of NEW AND RENEWABLE ENERGY 
be pleased to state:  
(a)  whether it is a fact that there is no policy for compulsory use of minimum quantity of 
renewable energy; 
(b)  if so, whether Government proposes to frame such a policy; 
(c)  if so, the details thereof; and 
(d)  if not, the reasons therefor? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINISTRY OF NEW AND RENEWABLE ENERGY  
(SHRI VILAS MUTTEMWAR): (a) to (d) Yes, Sir. However, under the Electricity Act 2003, 
the National Electricity Policy 2005 and the Tariff Policy 2006, it is bligatory upon State 
Electricity Regulatory Commissions to fix a certain percentage for purchase of power from 
renewable energy sources in the area of a distribution licensee. Such percentage is termed 
as Renewable Purchase Obligation. Accordingly, regulators in several States have issued 
Orders for Renewable Purchase Obligation varying from 1% to 10%. The details are given in 
the enclosed Statement.

Projects for generation of solar energy  
 * 488. SHRI K. CHANDRAN PILLAI: Will the Minister of NEW AND 
RENEWABLE ENERGY be pleased to state:  
(a)  the details of the projects for generation of solar energy in the country, State-wise; 
(b)  the volume of energy generated from this source during the last three years, year-
wise; 
(c)  whether the Ministry has any plans to increase the generation; and 
(d)  if so, the details of the plans for enhancing the generation of solar energy? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINISTRY OF NEW AND RENEWABLE ENERGY 
(SHRI VILAS MUTTEMWAR): (a) and (b) A total of 33 grid interactive solar Photovoltaic 
power plants have been installed in the country with financial assistance from the Ministry. 
A State-wise list of the plants is given in the Statement (See below). These plants, with 
aggregate capacity of 2.125 Megawatt peak (MWp), are estimated to generate about 
2.5 million units of electricity in a year. During the last three years the total generation is 
estimated to be about 7.5 million units.  
(c) and (d) Recently the Ministry has announced a demonstration programme to support 
mega watt size grid interactive solar power generation projects for a total capacity of 
50 MW, in the country. Any registered company, as project developer, is eligible to set up 
solar power projects on build, own and operate basis. Proposal from each project developer 
with a maximum aggregate capacity of 5 MW, either through a single project or multiple 
projects of a minimum capacity of 1 MW each, are to be considered for incentive.  
A maximum of 10 MW capacity solar power generation projects could be considered in 
State. Preference is to be given to the projects from the States where the State Electricity 
regulatory Commissions (SERCs) have announced or are in the process of announcing 
tariff for solar power.  
For the projects approved and commissioned by 31 st December, 2009, the Ministry will 
provide generation based incentive upto Rs. 12 per kWh for solar photovoltaic power and 
Rs. 10 per kWh for solar thermal power fed to the grid by the solar power project developers, 
ifter taking into account the tariff provided by the SERC or the utility. The Ministry will also 
provide incentive to the concerned utility and the State Nodal Agency, which will be involved 
in implementation and monitoring of the projects in that State.

*489. DR. EJAZ ALI: Will the Minister of HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT be 
pleased to state:  
(a)  whether Government is going to implement the 27 per cent reservation for OBCs in 
higher educational institutions, including IIMs and IITs, during 2008-09, after the Supreme 
Court's verdict; 
(b)  whether Government is going to increase the income range of creamy layer, currently 
put at Rs. 2.5 lakhs; 
(c)  if so, what would be the revised limit; and 
(d)  if not the reasons therefor? 
THE MINISTER OF HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT (SHRI ARJUN SINGH): 
(a) Yes, Sir, the Government have issued directions to Central Educational Institutions to 
implement reservation in admissions from the forthcoming academic session, as per the 
provisions of Central Educational Institutions (Reservation in Admission) Act, 2006 and in 
accordance with the directions of Supreme Court of India in this regard.  
(b) to (d) The Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment has entrusted the task of 
reviewing the existing income criterion used for determining the "creamy layer" from among 
the Other Backward Classes (OBCs), to the National Commission for Backward Classes 
(NCBC) vide that Ministry's order No. F 12015/13/2007-BCC December, 2007.

NTPC'sbidforUMPPs  
♦491. SHRI B.K. HARIPRASAD: Will the Minister of POWER be pleased to state:  
(a)  whether the National Thermal Power Corporation (NTPC), with its excellent record of 
successful start-ups and efficient operations of some major thermal power plants in the country, 
has not bagged even a single bid for Ultra Mega Power Projects (UMPPs) so far; 
(b)  whether the reason for NTPC losing out to private bidders for UMPPs is distortion in equity 
norms, to the disadvantage of an ethical entity like NTPC; and 
(c)  if so, the details thereof? 
THE MINISTER OF POWER (SHRI SUSHIL KUMAR SHINDE): (a) Out of the three Ultra Mega 
Power Projects (UMPPs) awarded so far, NTPC Ltd. had participated in the bidding of Sasan 
UMPP; but the company was not successful in getting the project;  
(b) and (c) For evaluating the bids in the tariff based bidding process, only the tariff quoted 
by the bidders is considered for determining the successful bidder. The bidding process does not 
require any bidder to disclose and/or submit detail s of either cost of project (Capital cost, 
Operation and Maintenance cost etc.) or its financing that is Debt-Equity ratio, return on equity 
etc. The bidder has to make own assessment of various costs involved and submit only the tariff 
in accordance with the provisions of bid documents. 
NTPC Ltd. could not win the bid as the evaluated levellised tariff of their tariff quote was not 
the lowest one, occasioned by various factors inclu ding the plant & equipment costs, 
performance parameters, financial parameters including cost of equity etc. The bid is a 
commercial decision of the bidding entity.  
Atrocities against women  
* 492. SHRIMATI BRINDA KARAT: Will the Minister of WOMEN AND CHILD 
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:  
(a)  the number of cases of atrocities against women registered during the last three years,

has developed a scheme for providing financial assistance for establishment of Mega Food 
Parks, which envisages a well-defined agri/horticultural-processing zone containing state 
of the art processing facilities with support infrastructure and well established supply 
chain. The scheme aims to provide a mechanism to bring together farmers, processors and 
retailers and link agricultural production to the market so as to ensure maximization of value 
addition, minimization of wastages and improving farmers' income. The primary objective of 
the scheme is to facilitate establishment of an integrated value chain, with processing at the 
core and supported by requisite backward and forward linkages. The ownership and 
management of the Mega Food Park would vest with a Special Purpose Vehicle (SPV) in 
which organized retailers, processors, service providers, farmers etc. may be the equity 
holders or there may be an anchor investor along with its ancillaries, associated companies 
and others stakeholders. The government agencies may also be shareholders in SPV upto 
a maximum of 49%.  
The scheme is project oriented. The locations of the Mega Food Parks have to be 
selected on a demand driven, cluster-based approach with delineated supply chain and well 
supported by pre-feasibility studies. Mega Food Parks can be established for any sector on 
need and viability basis such as fruit and vegetables, dairy, meat and poultry etc. or it can 
also have a combination of fruits and vegetables, dairy, meat and poultry etc. the decision 
on which will be taken by the Special Purpose Vehicle (SPV).  
The scheme intends to incentivise the private sector investment in creating food 
processing infrastructure in a big way. Accordingly, the Scheme envisages financial 
assistance in the form of grant-in-aid upto 50% of the project cost in general areas and upto 
75% of the project cost in special category states subject to a maximum of Rs. 50.00 crores 
or the cost of approved facilities, whichever is lower, for all implementing agencies including 
private sector. The scheme provides for establishment of 30 Mega Food Parks with MFPI 
financial assistance of Rs. 1500 crores during the 11th Five Year Plan.

Poultry processing plants  
3548. SHRI ABU ASIM AZMI: Will the Minister of FOOD  PROCESSING 
INDUSTRIES be pleased to state:  
(a)  whether Government has received any proposal for as sistance to set up poultry 
processing plants in various parts of the country; 
(b)  if so, the details thereof, State-wise particularly for Uttar Pradesh; 
(c)  whether the processing can screen and detect the Bi rd Flu that affected/is affecting 
the birds; and 
(d)  if so, the details in this regard? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINISTRY OF FOOD PROCESSING INDUSTRIES 
(SHRISUBODH KANT SAHAY): (a) to (d) Ministry of Food Processing Industries (MFPI) 
under its plan schemes, provides financial assistan ce, for Setting up/Modernization/ 
Expansion etc., of food processing units which incl udes mechanized/modern poultry 
processing plants also.  
MFPI has provided financial assistance to ten Mecha nized poultry processing units in 
Maharashtra (3), Karnataka (2), Kerala (2), Punjab (1), Haryana (1) and West Bengal (1) who 
applied for financial assistance under its plan sch eme. None of the proposals of Modern 
Poultry Processing plants have been received from U ttar Pradesh. During the 11th plan 
also, if proposals are received from the State(s), the Ministry will provide financial assistance 
to modernize poultry processing plants under its plan schemes.  
The mechanized poultry dressing process involves va rious stages which starts from 
ante-mortem inspection of the birds to finished pou ltry products by way of monitoring of 
each stage of processing. The ante-mortem inspection of the birds is being done by qualified 
Veterinarians who screen and reject the sick birds.  The detection of Bird flu infection is 
possible at farm level which has to be confirmed by  laboratory examination. Presently, 
screening/testing of sera for Avian Influenza (Bird Flu) is restricted only to Regional Disease 
Diagnostic Laboratories (RDDLs) and sera and Morbid  samples at High Security Animal 
Disease Diagnostic Laboratory (HSADL), Bhopal. However, the various stages of poultry 
processing such as scalding at 150C water temperatu re and 50-60 PPM of Chlorine for 
carcass washing inactivates the virus. Further, str ict Biosecurity measures and hygienic 
conditions in the processing plant can prevent spread of "Bird flu" infection in the processing 
plant.

be pleased to state:  
(a)  whether the domain of farming is enlarging from grain production to food processing, 
as there is a pressing need for trained manpower in rural and semi-urban areas; 
(b)  whether IGNOU, alongwith the Ministry is introducin g courses, targeting post harvest 
management and food processing activities, to dovertial growth in food processing industry; 
(c)  whether Government has formulated several schemes for enhancing growth in the segment, 
therefore the availability of trained manpower is the need of the hour; and

this sector? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINISTRY OF FOOD PROCESSING INDUSTRIES (SHRI 
SUBODH KANT SAHAY): (a) Yes Sir, it is true that th e domain of farming is enlarging from 
production to food processing since all the agricul ture produce are subjected to primary

UGC grants to Andhra Pradesh  
3554. SHRI PENUMALLI MADHU: Will the Minister of HU MAN RESOURCE 
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:  
(a)  the details of U.G.C. grants released to Andhra Pradesh during 2006-07 and 2007-08.

THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT 
(SHRIMATI D. PURANDESWARI): (a) to (c) According to the University Grants Commission 
(UGC), it has released Rs. 70.98 crore in 2006-07 and Rs. 23.82 crore in 2007-08 to universities

maintenance grants are given) as well as institutions 'deemed-to-be-universities' which are

based on parameters laid down by the Commission from time to time. Universities/Colleges 
located in educationally backward areas and young u niversities are given special 
development grants by the Commission.

Shutting down of NCTE  
3556. SHRIMATI SHOBHANA BHARTIA: Will the Minister of HUMAN RESOURCE 
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:  
(a)  whether the Ministry has on one side decided to shut down the National Council for 
Teacher Education (NCTE) and on the another side advertised for the appointment to the post of 
its Chairman and Vice-chairman; 
(b)  if so, the facts and the details thereof; 
(c)  whether Government proposes to seek the advice of other concerned Ministries and State 
Governments in this regard; and 
(d)  if so, the details thereof? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT 
(SHRI MD. ALIASHRAF FATMI): (a) to (d) A Review Committee under the Chairmanship of 
Shri Sudeep Banerjee, the then Advisor, Ministry of  Human Resource Development was 
appointed to conduct an indepth study of the National Council for Teacher Education (NCTE), 
New Delhi and its Regional Offices. The Committee observed inter-alia that the functioning of 
NCTE was not commensurate with the objective of planned and coordinated development of 
Teacher Education and recommended that the NCTE Act, 1993 should be repealed and all 
regulatory functions relating to teacher edcuation and teacher education institutions should be 
vested in the University system. After inter-ministerial consultations the Legislative Department 
under the Ministry of Law & Justice has been requested to draft the 'Repeal Bill'. Meanwhile, the 
posts of Chairperson and Vice-Chairperson, NCTE have fallen vacant. Processes have been 
initiated to fill up the vacancies.

of 6 to 14 years has been mandated in our Constitution as a fundamental right;

role. The Government is committed to facilitate the enactment of an appropriate legislation 
that would enable the realization of making educati on a fundamental right as required by

Illiterates in the country  
3579. DR. ABHISHEK MANU SINGHVI: Will the Minister of HUMAN RESOURCE 
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:  
(a)  whether it is a fact that one-third of the world's illiterates are in this country, according 
to a UNESCO report released in November, 2007, and the downward trend is persisting as 
the country has slipped five ranks since the last y ear to 105 on the global education 
parameters;

children; and 
(c)  if not, the steps being adopted therefor? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT 
(SHRI MD. ALI ASHRAF FATMI): (a) and (b) Yes Sir, India has 35% of the world's total 
illiterates. Even though India has been ranked 105 tn  in the Global Monitoring Report (GMR), 
2008, as compared to 99th rank in the GMR, 2007, the Education Development Index (EDI) 
has risen from 0.789 to 0.797.  
The main achievements of India, as per the GMR 2008, are high level of net enrolment in 
Primary education and significantly improved adult literacy and gender parity.  
The following concrete steps have been taken for achieving the Millennium Development 
Goal pertaining to universal primary education:  
(i) Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan (SSA) aimed at achieving the objectives of universalization 
of elementary education amongst children in the age group of 6-14 years in a time 
bound manner. As a result of this programme a large number of children have been 
brought into the fold of elementary education and number of out of school children 
has come down from 320 lakh in 2001-02 to 76 lakh in 2007-08.  
(ii) Introduction to cooked Mid-day Meal (MDM) Scheme for all children in class I-V 
in Government and Government aided schools, centres under the Alternating and 
Innovative Education (A1E) and Education Guarantee Scheme and its extension to 
upper Primary level in 3479 educationally backward blocks (EBBs).  
(iii) Levy of 2% Education Cess in order to bridge the gap between available plan 
resources and established requirements to finance S arva Shiksha Abhiyan and 
Mid-day Meal, the two main programmes for universal ization of elementary 
education.  
(c) Does not arise.

Judge-population ratio  
3623. SHRI GIREESH KUMAR SANGHI: Will the Minister of LAW AND JUSTICE be 
pleased to state:  
(a)  the number of Judges per million population of the country; 
(b)  what is the number of Judges per million, suggested by the apex court; 
(c)  what steps the Ministry is taking to comply with the order; and 
(d)  whether Government would earmark court fee levied by States exclusively for Judicial 
kitty to augment the strength of Judges? 
THE MINISTER OF LAW AND JUSTICE (SHRI H.R. BHARDWAJ): (a) to (c) The Law 
Commission in its 120th Report recommended that the strength of judges per million 
population may be increased from 10.5 to 50 judges. The present judge strength in India 
is 14 per million population (approx.). Government has already increased the Judge strength 
in the High Courts by 152.  
With regard to subordinate judiciary, the Supreme Court, in its judgment of 21" March, 
2002, in All India Judges' Association & Ors Vs. Union of India & Ors., directed that 
an increase in the Judge strength from the existing  10.5 per 10 lakh people to 50 
judges per 10 lakh people should be effected and implemented within a period of five 
years in a phased manner to be determined and direc ted by the Union Ministry of 
Law. The Central Government have filed an affidavit in the Supreme Court praying 
that the increase in judge strength in the Union Territories for which Central Government 
is administratively responsible be allowed based on workload and pendency of cases. 
The matter is sub-judice. As directed by the apex court, the Central Government also 
filed an affidavit indicating the quantum of funds required in compliance of the 
aforesaid Supreme Court's judgment irrespective of the category of funds that will be 
drawn.  
All State Governments are also party to this case. Under article 235 of the Constitution of 
India, the administrative control over the members of subordinate judiciary in the States 
vests with the concerned High Court and the State Government. Accordingly, the Central 
Government has requested all the State Governments for taking necessary action to increase 
the judge strength as per the direction of the Supreme Court and also to fill up the vacant 
posts of judicial officers on urgent basis.  
(d) There is no such proposal before the Government.

3628.   SHRI AMAR SINGH: SHRI ABU 
AS1MAZMI: Will die Minister of LAW AND JUSTICE be

(c) what action Government has taken thereon?  
THE MINISTER OF LAW AND JUSTICE (SHRI H. R. BHARDWAJ): (a) to (c) In their 
meeting held on 10.1.2008, thenar Council of Delhi observed that the Judicial Officers who 
were above the age of 58'^ years were not considere d for elevation as Judges of the Delhi 
High Court and expressed the view that the Constitution of India does not provide- for any 
classification of age and that in the matters of ap pointment of Judges to the High Court, 
Article 217 of the Constitution of India cannot be overlooked and any policy, written or 
otherwise, to this effect is inherently unconstitutional.  
2.  The Bar Council of India considered the above resolution of the Delhi Bar Council and 
informed the Delhi Bar Council that they resolve an d agree with the sentiments expressed 
and the logic and reasoning behind the resolution and that there is no justification in fixing 
up the above limit. The Bar Council of India also informed the Bar Council of Delhi that the 
prescription of upper age limit is unreasonable and would only help to supersede the most 
experienced judges. 
3.  In the Conference of Chief Ministers and Chief Just ices held on 4.12.1993, it was 
decided that a District Judge elevated as a Judge of the High Court should have the prospect 
of serving at least 3 years on the Bench. Accordingly, the Chief Justices of the High Courts 
were requested to initiate proposals at least 6 months prior to a Judicial officer attaining the 
age of 59 years so that even if 6 months are taken in processing the proposal, the person will 
have 3 years clear tenure on the Bench. 
4.  In consultation with the Chief Justice of India, in September, 2004, it was decided that 
a Judicial Officer shall be eligible for being considered for elevation as a Judge of the High 
Court if he is or was within the prescribed age limit of 581/2 years or below on the date of 
occurrence of the vacancy against which he is being  considered, irrespective of when the 
Collegium recommends him for elevation as a Judge of the High Court. 
5.  There is no proposal before the Government to make any change in the present 
system.

Installed capacity of wind power  
3636. DR. M.A.M. RAMASWAMY. Will the Minister of NEW AND RENEWABLE 
ENERGY be pleased to state:  
(a)  the total installed capacity of wind power in our country, as on date, State-wise; 
(b)  how much wind power has been added during the last three years, State-wise and 
year-wise; 
(c)  whether our country's wind power addition is abysmally low, as compared to China, 
USA and Spain; 
(d)  if so, the reasons for such a low addition; and 
(e)  the steps taken or propsed to be taken to generate more wind power in the country? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINISTRY OF NEW AND RENEWABLE ENERGY 
(SHRI VILAS MUTTEMWAR): (a) A total Wind Power capacity of 8753 MW has been 
installed in the country, till 31 st March, 2008. State-wise details are given in Statement-I (See 
below).  
(b)  A total Wind Power capacity of 5118 MW has been installed in the country during the 
last three years. State-wise details are given in Statement-II (See below). 
(c)  and (d) No, Sir. A wind power capacity 15120 MW were added during the year 2007 
worldwide. While the contributions from USA, Spain and China were 5216 MW, 3515 MW 
and 3313 MW respectively, the wind power capacity addition in India during 2007 was 
1580 MW which was comparable to the capacity addition during 2006 which was about 
1840MW. 
(e) Steps taken by the Government to encourage setting up of wind power projects in the 
country are concessional import duty on certain components of wind electric generator; 
excise duty exemption, ten years' tax holiday on income generated from wind power projects; 
benefit of accelerated depreciation; loan from Indian Renewable Energy Development 
Agency (IREDA) and other financial institutions; policies in the States for grid connection 
and sale of electricity generated; technical support by the Centre for Wind Energy 
Technology (C-WET) including detailed wind resource assessment to identify further 
potential sites.

Solar energy generation  
3639. SHRl N.R. GOVINDARAJAR: Will the Minister of NEW AND RENEWABLE 
ENERGY be pleased to state:  
(a)  the quantum of solar energy generated in the country, as on date; 
(b)  whether Government proposes to give priority to solar energy over hydro and thermal 
power, as the cost of production of solar energy is very less; 
(c)  if so, the details thereof; 
(d)  the fund allocated to each state to popularize solar energy during the last three years; and 
(e)  the details of manufacturers of solar energy systems in each State, as on date? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINISTRY OF NEW AND RENEWABLE ENERGY 
(SHRI VILAS MUTTEM WAR): (a) to (c) Solar energy can be harnessed through two routes, namely 
solar photovoltaic (PV) and solar thermal. In photovoltaic route, it is directly converted to electricity 
while in solar thermal route it is first converted into heat and then to electricity.  
A total of 33 grid interactive solar photovoltaic p ower plants have been installed in the 
country with financial assistance from the Ministry. These plants, with aggregate capacity of 
2.125 Megawatt peak (MWp), are estimated to generate about 2.5 million units of electricity in a 
year.  
In addition, the solar energy systems are being used for stand-alone applications in lighting, 
telecommunication, small power requirements, battery charging, water heating and cooking etc. So 
far around 14.5 lakh solar photovoltaic systems agg regating to about 125 Megawatt peak 
solar photovoltaic module capacity have been installed in the country. Further, about 6.15 lakh 
solar cookers and about 23 lakh square metre collector area has been installed for solar water 
heating applications, which is equivalent to about 1600 Megawatt thermal capacity.  
The utilization of solar energy in the country is regularly increasing, however, the high initial 
cost of the solar energy systems is a barrier in its large-scale utilization. The estimated cost of 
electricity from grid connected solar energy plant is around Rs. 12-15 per unit, which is high 
compared to electricity generated from conventional sources including thermal power and 
other renewable energy sources such as wind, small hydro and biomass.  
Recently, a new demonstration scheme has been announced by the Ministry to provide 
generation based incentive for MW-capacity grid int eractive solar power projects in the 
country.  
(d)  The details of state-wise release of funds during the last three years for various solar 
energy programmes are given in Statement-I {See below). 
(e)  The State-wise details of manufacturers of solar photovoltaic (SPV) cells/modules, flat 
plate collector (FPC) and evacuated tube collector (ETC) based solar water heating systems 
and solar cookers are given in Statement-I I.

Tripping of Northern Grid  
3648. SHRI MAHENDRA MOHAN: Will the Minister of POWER be pleased to state:  
(a)  whether it is a fact that Northern Grid has again near about collapsed, this time due to excess 
power supply, as demand dipped due to sudden rain in the Northern region; 
(b)  if so, the details thereof; 
(c)  whether some States are drawing excess power from the Northern Grid stating the demand 
and supply position of different States drawing power from the Northern Grid; and 
(d)  what has been done to ensure safety of the Grid and back up supply in case of failure? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF POWER (SHRI JAIRAM RAMESH): (a) and 
(b) There was reduction in demand by about 4700 MW in Northern Region during  

Written Answers  [28 APRIL,2008]        to Unstarred Questions   135  
the early morning hours of 3 ,d  April 2008 due to rain. The reduction in demand was handled by 
reducing import of 1500 MW power, exporting 1400 M W power to neighbouring regions and 
backing down 1450 MW generation at coal and gas stations in Northern Region. The marginal 
surplus resulted in system frequency in the range of 50-50.2 Hz., which was within  
permissible limit.  
(c)  There is a continuing shortage of power in the Northern Region, leading to overdraw of 
power from the grid by the states with a view to increase availability of power. All the states in 
Northern Region except Delhi, Himachal Pradesh and Union Territory of Chandigarh had over-
drawn from the grid during March, 2008. 
(d)  As per provisions of Electricity Act, 2003, Regiona l Load Dispatch Centres 
continuously monitor and take necessary actions to maintain the security of the Regional Grids in 
real time. The operational matters concerning stability and smooth operation of the Regional Grids 
are also discussed regularly in the respective Regional Power Committee. 
Regarding back-up supply in case of failure, mock exercises for black-stait of hydro units, 
islanded operation and synchronization with main Grid are done, by Regional Load Dispatch 
Centres, periodically, to test the readiness of equipment as well as operating  
personnel.

advanced power evacuation system. These include thei800 kV, High voltage Direct Current 
(HVDC) transmission technology and 1200 kV Ultra High Voltage (UHV) AC technology.  
(c) to (e) Fort 800 kV HVDC technology, preliminary  studies with respect to HVDC

stations etc. have been completed. Similarly, other technical studies regarding insulation levels, 
requirement for HVDC controls, interaction studies with existing schemes etc. have been 
accomplished. Based on the results of these studies, design and technical specifications have been 
prepared. The requisite tests necessary before actual implementation shall be conducted. This

Reorganisation of State Electricity Boards  
3656. DR. K. MALAISAMY: Will the Minister of POWER be pleased to state:  
(a)  whether there is any move in the State Electricity Boards to divide and make them into 
two or three separate organizations; 
(b)  if so, the reasons therefor; and 
(c)  whether, in that process, there has been stiff opposition both from within and outside 
on the ground that the co-ordination and the purpose of service would be lost? 

Written Answers  [28 APRIL, 2008]        to Unstarred Questions    143  
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF POWER (SHRI JAIRAM RAMESH): (a) to 
(c) With the coming into force of the Electricity Act, 2003, and the consequent repeal of the 
earlier Central Acts of the power sector the Electricity Boards (SEBs) constituted under the 
repealed Acts were, under the provisions of Section  172 (a) of the Electricity Act, 2003, 
deemed to be the State Transmission Utilities and Licensees for a period upto one year, and 
thereafter for such further period as may be mutually decided upon by the Central Government 
and the concerned State Government. Section 172(c) of the Electrictiy Act, 2003 further 
provides that the undertakings of SEBs may, after the expiry of the period specified in Section 
172 (a), be transferred in accordance with the provisions of Part XIII of the Electricity Act, 
2003. Part XIII of the Act provides for transfer by the State Government of any property, interest 
in property, rights and liabilities of SEBs to a Government company or in a company or companies 
in terms of the provisions of that Part.  
Thirteen States have so far reorganized their SEBs. Ten States (Orissa, Haryana, Andhra Pradesh, 
Karnataka, Uttar Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Rajasthan, Delhi, Gujarat and Madhya Pradesh) had 
reorganized their SEBs under their respective State Electricity Reform Acts, enacted before 
enactment of the Electricity Act, 2003. Assam, Maharashtra and West Bengal have reorganized 
their SEBs under the provisions of the Electricity Act, 2003. Government of Tripura has 
corporatized its Electricity Department.  
Eight States (Bihar, Jharkhand, Kerala, Punjab, Chhattisgarh, Tamil Nadu, Meghalaya and 
Himachal Pradesh) have been requesting the Central Government under Section 172(a) of the 
Electricity Act, 2003 to agree for extensions of time for reorganization of their respective SEBs, 
which have been agreed to.  
According to information received from Government of Chhattisgarh, there is opposition from 
officers and employees unions of Chhattisgarh State Electricity Board (CS.EB); in Jharkhand, 
there is some resistance among employees.

 Rise in prices of Naphtha  
 
3666. SHRI K. CHANDRAN PILLA1: Will the Ministerof POWER be pleased to state:  
(a) whether it is a fact that there is a steep rise in  T he prices of Naphtha;  
(b) if so, whether this increase has raised the cost units;  of power generation in  Naphtha 
based  
(c) if so, the details thereof;  

Written Answers  [28 APRIL, 2008]        to Unstarred Questions    161  
(d)  whether Government proposes to exempt Naphtha from excise duty to tide over the 
present crisis faced by Naphtha based power units in the country; and 
(e)  if not, what steps Government proposes to protect t hese power generating units? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF POWER (SHRIJAKAM RAMESH ): 
(a) Yes, Sir. The price of Naphtha has increased fr om Rs. 34,898/Metric Tonne (MT) in 
March, 2007 to Rs. 46,148/MT in March, 2008.  
(b) and (c) Yes, Sir. The increase in price of Naph tha has resulted in an increase in the 
variable cost component of the cost of generation i n Naphtha based power plants. The 
variable component of the average cost of sale of energy has gone up from Rs. 5.96/kWh in  
•  2006-07 to Rs. 7.37/kWh in 2007-08 (Provisional)  in the case of Rajiv Gandhi Combined 
Cycle Power Station of NTPC Ltd.  
(d) and (e) No, Sir. At present there is no proposal under consideration of Government to 
exempt Naphtha for generation of power from Excise duty. As the domestic price of Naphtha, 
which is determined based on its international price, has increased steeply, power generating 
units based on Naphtha, are increasingly opting for  Re-gasified Liquefied Natural Gas 
(RLNG) so as to minimize the variable cost of generation of such units.

3669. DR. T. SUBBARAMI REDDY: Will the the Minister of POWER be pleased to state:  
(a)  whether Government proposes to allow private compan ies to develop hydropower 
projects on cost-sharing basis, instead of tariff-b ased bidding, bringing the private power 
players on par with the public sector peers; 
(b)  if so, whether this dispensation is currently available only to PSUs, till January, 2011; 
(c)  whether section 63 of the Electricity Act, 2003 provides for development of projects 
on competitive bidding for tariff, when the project is awarded to the lowest bidder; and 
(d)  if so, by when a final decision in this regard is likely to be taken? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF POWER (SHRI JAIRAM RAMESH): 
(a) to (b) In a recent amendment to the Tariff Policy, subject to fulfillment of certain conditions, 
the private sector projects have also been allowed the same dispensation of exemption from 
tariff based bidding upto January, 2011, as was available to public sector projects.  
(c)  Section 63 of the Electricity Act, 2003 already provides that the appropriate commission 
shall adopt the tariff if such tariff has been dete rmined through a transparent process of 
bidding in accordance with the guidelines issued by the Central Government. 
(d)  Does not arise in view of (c) above.

3670. SHRI PENUMALLI MADHU: Will the the Minister of SOCIAL JUSTICE AND

management falls within the administrative jurisdiction of the State Governments as provided 
under Entry No. 18 of the State List (List II) of t he Seventh Schedule to the Constitution. 
The role of the Central Government in this field is  only of an advisory and coordinating 
nature. However, implementation of land reforms programmes is reviewed from time to time 
at various fora, including Conferences of the Reven ue Ministers/Secretaries of States and 
UTs organized by the Ministry of Rural Development. The State Governments have, inter-
alia, been requested from time to time for distribution of ceiling surplus land, Govt, waste 
land and Bhoodan land to the eligible rural poor by  preparation of action plans, and to 
complete the task by undertaking special drives.  
As per the information received from the States, on  implementation of the land ceiling 
laws, an area of 68.59 lakh acres has been declared surplus, of which 59.98 lakh acres has 
been taken possession of, and 49.68 lakh acres has been distributed to 55.34 lakh beneficiaries,

Training, Grant-in-aid is provided to 18 Tribal Research Institutes on 50 : 50 basis between

teaching materials for the tribals and surveying of tribal Dialects to prepare linguisitic and culture

Definition of Child  
3691. SHRI M.V. MYSURA REDDY: Will the Minister of WOMEN AND CHILD 
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:  
(a)  whether it is a fact that the definition of 'Child'  in different Acts in the country 
gives a different meaning and is thereby creating problems to law enforcing agencies; and 
(b)  why the country does not wish to conform to the UN Convention Norm on the 
definition of 'Child'? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINISTRY OF WOMEN AND CHILD 
DEVELOPMENT (SHRIMATI RENUKACHOWDHURY): (a) and (b) A child is defined as a 
person below the age of 18 years in the UN Convention on the Rights of the Child. Definition 
of child varies in our country from legislation to legislation according to its nature and 
scope. The Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2000 has the same definition 
of the 'Child' as the UN Convention on the Rights o f the Child. At present there is no 
proposal to make definition of the 'Child' uniform in all other legislations.

3692. SHRIMATI SUPRIYA SULE: 
SHRIMATI KANIMOZHI:  
Will the Minister of WOMEN AND CHILD DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:  
(a)  whether, with two million children under the age of five dying every year, the country 
has a dismal record in child mortality; 
(b)  whether a new study conducted by Save the Children, which compares child mortality 
in a country to its national income per person, sho ws that India lags behind poorer 
neighbourers like Bangladesh and Nepal when it comes to cutting child deaths; 
(c)  if so, what are the other main features of the report; and 
(d)  what steps are being taken in this regard? 

Written Answers  [28 APRIL,2008]  to Unstarred Questions    177  
THE MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINISTRY OF WOMEN AND CHILD 
DEVELOPMENT (SHRIMATI RENUKACHOWDHURY): (a) As per the UNICEF report 
titled "The State of the World's Children-2008", two million children under the age of five, 
died in the country during year 2006.  
(b)  As per Save the Children report titled "State of the World's Mother-2007: Saving the 
Lives of Children Under 5" the Under-5 mortality rate in India is 74 per thousand live births 
while in Bangladesh it is 73 per thousand live birt hs and in Nepal 74 per thousand live 
births. 
(c)  The key findings of the report reveals that an alarming number of countries are failing 
to make progress in saving children's lives and in many places the situation is getting 
worse; millions of children's lives may be saved by  Way of low-cost basic interventions; 
child and maternal death rates are highest in the p oorest and most disadvantaged places 
and the countries that save children's lives also i mprove their prospects for economic 
growth and social development. 
The Recommendations of the report are:  
* Ensure the well-being of mothers 
* Invest in basic, low-cost solutions to save children's lives. 
* Expand the availability of health care to the poorest and most vulnerable mothers 
and children. 
* Increase funding and improve strategies to increase the use of basic, life saving 
services known. 
* Increase government support for proven solutions that save the lives of mothers, 
children and newborns. 
(d) The Ministry of Health and Family Welfare and t he Ministry of Women and Child 
Development, Government of India have taken the fol lowing measures to improve the 
situation of infant and child mortality:  
(i)  Integrated management of Neonatal and childhood ill esses.  
(ii)  Home based newborn care.  
(iii)  Promotion of breastfeeding and complementary feeding.  
(iv)  Control of deaths due to acute respiratory Infections.  
(v)  Control of deaths due to diarrhoeal diseases.  
(vi)  Supplementation with micronutrients; Vitamin A and Iron.  
(vii)  Universal Immunization Programme.  
(viii)  Several other National Health Programme under NRHM. 
(ix)  Implementation of the Integtrated Child Development Services (ICDS) Scheme.

STATEMENT BY MINISTER  
Successful launch often satellites by India's Polar Satellite launch vehicle (PSLV-C9)  
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE PRIME MINISTER'S OFFICE AND THE MINISTER 
OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PERSONNEL, PUBLIC GRIEVANCES AND PENSIONS 
(SHRI PRITHVIRAJ CHAVAN): Sir, I am happy to inform this August House that, today 
(April 28, 2008), India's Polar Satellite Launch Vehicle (PSLV-C9) successfully launched 
CARTOSAT-2A, Indian Mini Satellite-1 (IMS-1) and eight nano satellites for international 
customers into the desired orbit. This is the 12th consecutively successful flight of PSLV 
conducted from Satish Dhawan Space Centre (SDSC), S hriharikota. All the systems have 
performed satisfactorily. PSLV-C9 launched in its c ore alone configuration launched ten 
satellites with a total weight of about 820 kilogra ms.  
CARTOSAT-2A weighing 690 kilograms is  a state-of-the-art Remote Sensing Satellite, 
similar to CARTOSAT-2 launched on January 10,2007. The data with a resolution of about 
one metre from this satellite will used for detailed mapping applications at cadastral level, 
urban and rural infrastructure development and mana gement.  
Along with CARTOSAT-2A, 83 kilogram Indian Mini Sat ellite-1 (IMS-1) which 
incorporates many new technologies and has miniatur e sub-systems was also launched 
successfully. The data from this mission will be made available to interested space agencies 
and student community from developing countries to provide necessary impetus to capacity 
building in using satellite data.  

206    Matter raised  [RAJYA SABHA]  with permission  
Eight nano satellites launched onboard PSLV-C9 were  built by Universities and 
research institutions in Canada and Cosmos International, Germany.  
This successful launch, of PSLV-C9 has reiterated its reliability and versatility to launch 
satellites in various types of orbits and also to c arry out multiple satellite missions. I am 
sure that this august House will join me in congrat ulating the Chairman, ISRO, and his 
team on this magnificent achievement.

SHR RAMACHANDRA KHUNTIA (Orissa): Mr. Deputy Chairman, Sir, although many 
steps have been taken to curb this deadliest diseas e of malaria in the country, still this 
disease is spreading more dangerously. There was a news item in the Times of India on 
the deadliest disease of malaria which is becoming more and more dangerous. Therefore, 
I request the Government to take appropriate steps to curb this deadliest disease in this 
counry. Thank you.

Statement made by the Minister of Shipping, Road Tr ansport and Highways in 
the House on 23rd April, 2008  
DR. V. MAITREYAN (Tamil Nadu): On 23rd morning, I wanted to raise an issue arising 
out a news report in the New Indian Express of Chennai. The hon. Chairman was kind 
enough to permit me to raise that issue during the Zero Hour, and I thank him for that. And, 
when I did raise that issue during the Zero Hour, t he hon. Minister of Surface Transport, 
Shri T.R. Baalu, was kind enough to be present here , and he was generous enough to 
respond to the submission which I made. And, I am thankful to him for having spoken the 
truth in the House on that day. Sir, the hon. Minis ter, while speaking, in response to the 
submission that I made, openly accepted that he did  put in a word to his colleague, the 
Minister of Petroleum and Natural Gas, and that there was nothing wrong in it. In fact, the 
Minister has been truthful, but the Prime Minister's Office has not been truthful. The Prime 
Minister's Office has written eight letters in the last six months. When I wanted to raise this 
issue on the next day when the Prime Minister was supposed to be there and the concerned 
Minister was also there, I could not do so. Just be cause I could not raise the issue, it does 
not mean that the issue has died down. The issues are very much pertinent even today. The 
issues are being talked over in the television channels. The issues are being talked over in 
the media. The pertinent issues are: No. 1; Shri T.R. Baalu did admit in the House that he 
influenced ..(Interuptions)...  
MR. DEPUTY CHAIRMAN: No interruptions, please. It i s a Zero Hour mention 
...(Interruptions)... That has been allowed.  
DR. V. MAITREYAN: So, I seek and explanation from the Prime Minister's Office, and 
from the Prime Minister, as to what their response is to the open acceptance by the Minister 
on the floor of the House. No. 2; we want an explan ation from the hon. Prime Minister 
regarding the various letters written from the PMO, whether they were with the knowledge 
or without the knowledge of the Prime Minister. Sir , the hon. Minister of Parliamentary 
Affairs Minister said that the Government would respond today.  
MR. DEPUTY CHAIRMAN: Not today. He has not said that.  
DR. V. MAITREYAN: I would only like to urge upon th e hon. Parliamentary Affairs 
Minister to see to it that the Government gives its  response as early as possible because 
'Justice Delayed is Justice Denied'.

214   Special  [RAJYASABHA]  Mentions  
 
Death of four Babies at Tiruvallur Primary Health Centre in Tamiinadu 
due to Administration of Measle Vaccine  
SHRIMATI JAYANTHI NATARAJAN (Tamil Nadu): Sir, I rise to draw the attention of 
the House, through you, about the tragic incident of the death of four children in Tamil 
Nadu after the administration of measles vaccination. More than 52,000 are affected by 
measles every year and the immunisation programme is a very important programme in the 
country particularly with regard to children. These vaccines were administered through the 
Public Healti System and of course, Sir, the Tamil Nadu Government has taken all the steps 
to provide immediate relief and succour and the Tamil Nadu Government has also ordered 
an inquiry into the matter. The inquiry is going on. That is not the issue.  
The important issue which I want to raise is, Sir, the issue of vaccines, the storage of 
vaccines. I would like to know whether in private hospitals these vaccines are administered 
in a single dose whereas in Government hospitals, because of the cost involved, they are 
procured in large vials and some times they are used for 3-4 children and the question of 
storage and die breaking of the cold chain becomes very important with regard to the 
administration of these vaccines. Of course, the investigation will show whether the vaccines 
were defective, per se, or whether there" was a human error involved. But, I would like to 
emphasise, Sir, that in future, with regard to the administration of vaccines, every Public 
Health Centre must have provision of an emergency kit to treat reaction to vaccination and 
to drugs. The children are supposed to have died of anaphylactic shock. In a Public Health 
Centre, mere is no kit and there is no training of die staff in the Public Health Centres to treat 
children who have now suffered from an overdose of the drug or from a shock reaction to 
me drug. Immediately the children had to be taken to nearby Government hospitals, which 
actually increases the shock and it does not decrease the shock. The staff have to be 
trained to recognise also what an anaphylactic shock is, what an adverse reaction to the 
drug is and administer immediate first aid. 40 lakh doses of the same vaccine from die same 
company have now been withdrawn. Now, the public confidence in vaccination has been 
shaken. We cannot over-emphasise the importance of the vaccination in a country like 
India. In order to restore the public confidence, Sir, the Government should take immediate 
steps to ensure that the safe storage of vaccines happens and also that there is proper  

Special  [28 APRIL, 2008]  Mention   215  
training of staff in Public Health Centres to ensure that children and people do not die of 
shock or drug overdose. Thank you

Demand to take measures to write Orissa as Odissa i n all languages 
SHRI RAMA CHANDRA KHUNTIA (Orissa): The name of the State of Orissa has been 
changed to Odissa. But, unfortunately, when written  in English, it is still written as Orissa 
instead of Odissa, in all Government official recor ds as well as in die electronic and print 
media. Similarly, while writing in Hindi, it is wri tten as Udissa. This, is an insulting and a 
humiliating thing for us. Several NGOs and various Associations have been demanding that 
this mistake should be rectified. I myself have met the hon. Prime Minister and have given a 
memorandum in this regard. He has also assured us that he would look into the matter.  
I once again urge upon the Government of India and the State Government to take 
appropriate steps to rectify this mistake, while writing in English and Hindi, and see to it that 
it is written as Odissa, as it is done in all other languages.  
Demand to provide 'Z' category security for Dr. J. Jayalalitha, former 
Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu  
SHRI N.R. GOVINDARAJAR (Tamil Nadu): Sir I would like to bring to the notice of the 
Government the need for .'Z' Category Security for the former Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu, Dr. 
Jayalalitha. During her governance in Tamil Nadu, Dr. Jayalalitha took steps to control and 
eradicate the anti-social elements. Dr. Amma has been the one who consistently opposed the 
LITE at all times and tried to curb its activities in Tamil Nadu. Because of her strict governance 
against terrorist groups, Naxals and other miscreants, now there is a serious threat to her life. 
It is the duty of the Government to provide adequate protection to former Chief Ministers and 
other prominent leaders so that they could serve the society for long. Despite many requisitions 
made by the public, the present protection provided by the Government of Tamil Nadu is not 
adequate to tackle unwanted incidents and the secur ity personnel are untrained. It is not 
honourable for the largest democratic country in th e world, known for its integrity and 
administration, to thus treat such a prominent political leader who has spent her life serving 
the people of this country. Hence, I request the Go vernment to take necessary steps to 
immediately provide 'Z' Category Security to Dr. Ja yalalitha.  
SHRI S. ANBALAGAN (Tamil Nadu): Sir, I associate myself with the Special Mention 
made by the hon. Member.

216   Special  [RAJYASABHA]  Mention  
Demand for a separate Statutory Development Board for North 
Maharashtra  
SHRIMATI SUPRIYA SULE (Maharashtra): Sir, the Maharashtra Government had 
submitted a proposal for a separate Statutory Development Board for North Maharashtra 
on 26.2.2007 to the Government of India. Both the Houses of the State Legislature, on 
13th July, 2006 had unanimously passed a resolution for establishment of a separate Statutory 
Development Board for five districts of North Maharashtra viz., Dhule, Jalgaon, Nandurbar, 
Nashik and Ahmednagar. Accordingly, a proposal to amend article 371(2)(a) of the Indian 
Constitution was forwarded to the Union Home Ministry by the Maharashtra Government 
on 26.2.2007. In spite of the reminders sent to the Union Home Ministry on 6.7.2007 and 
18.9.2007,  no action has been taken so far in this proposal.  
I, therefore, urge upon the Government to kindly initiate the action by amending the 
Consititution so that the proposal of the Maharashtra Government is immediately accepted.

SHRI PRASANTA CHATTERJEE (West Bengal): India has six years of experience now 
with BT Cotton, a GE/GM crop. Even from official reports, it is apparent that the technology 
has not delivered on its promises. Worse, it has created new problems like allergies 
experienced by people harvesting BT cotton or deaths and illnesses of animals that have 
grazed on BT cotton fields. Newer pests and diseases are reported, including increase in 
sucking pests. More inputs like chemical fertilizers and irrigation are being applied on 
BT cotton, further eroding natural resources. All of this is seen in India even as more and 
more countries are banning GM crops elsewhere, adopting the precautionary principle. 
Emerging scientific data is constantly establishing , and reiterating the hazards of 
GM crops.  
In India, the Government is considering approval for the second year large-scale trials of 
BT brinjal, the first ever GM vegetable crop anywhere with the BT gene in it, being pushed 
into India by the U.S. companies. The impact of this BT brinjal are unpredictable and 
unknown. Biosafety data has been withheld from public scrutiny. There is no independent 
research done by the Govenment. ICAR research data shows better results with IPM based 
methods than with BT brinjal trials. Lakhs of organic farmers are controlling pests without 
the-use of pesticides or GE seeds. Why then is the Government keen on allowing BT brinjal? 
What will happen to consumer and farmer choices if they wish to remain GM-free? Who will 
be accountable for the potential hazards of this experimentation with all Indians? We demand 
that the Government disallow all trials on BT brinjal.

damages in the month of October-November, 2006. The Prime Minister was also requested

households who have lost their houses. The State has also drawn the attention of the 
Government that in the past similar sanctions have been given to the States, that is, Orissa 
and Bihar.

a proposal to the Government of India for leveraging the PMGSY to the tune of Rs. 900 
crores in the State. Definite sanctions have been obtained from the Banks for Rs. 500 crores 
and the projects have already been submitted to the Government of India. The Government

Wakf Development Corporation, to assess and monitor  the benefits actually reaching

Concern over Dismal performance of Indian Hockey  
SHRI BHARATKUMAR BHAVANISHANKAR RAUT (Maharashtra):  It is a 
matter of grave concern and shame that the Indian W omen Hockey Team is also out of 
the Olympic Games to be held in Beijing. The Men's team is already out of the 
Olympic Games.  
There was a time when India was the undisputed lead er in the world hockey. The 
Indian Women team had also won honours of Gold and Silver Medals in the past. 
However, the Indian Hockey is now passing through a  difficult phase.  
The time has come that all those who are concerned for Indian sports must sit 
together and think about the fate of the game that was once the pride of India. This 
thinking should be beyond the party-lines. All thos e who are responsible for bringing 
the situation to disrepute should be thrown out of the arena. This would bring a new 
life to the game.  
India is having a lot of talented young players wit h enthusiasm and exuberance. So 
what we need to do is to keep politics and dirt out  of the game. Hence, I request the hon. 
Minister of Youth Affairs and Sports to look into t his and ensure that the Indian Hockey 
regain its lost glory immediately. Thank you.

PROF. M.S. SWAMINATHAN (Nominated): Thank you very much, Mr. Chairman, Sir. 
First of all, this morning, we saluted our space sc ientists for making our nation proud, for 
their enormous contributions and, above all, for de monstrating that in our counry if we 
adopt a mission approach, or, in other words, if all links in a chain are attended to carefully 
and methodically, then we can succeed. We are proud  not only of their achievements but 
also of what they have shown about how to organise successful programmes.  
I would like to say this afternoon that we should also salute our farm women and men. I 
have now been working in agriculture for 64 years, 1944-onwards, I have seen in every part 
of our country, the very serious constrains under w hich our farm women and men work. I 
use the word farm women and men, particularly, because many times, farmer means only a 
man, but 70 per cent of the work is done by the wom en in the field. If you look at the 
difficulties under which they work—I am sure, the h on. Agriculture Minister will shortly be 
mentioning what kinds of achievements we have had in agriculture this year you will really 
wonder at the greatness and the hardship under whic h they work. I therefore, say in our 
House here, although it is now a very depleted House, we must salute our farm women and 
men of our country. They are really the saviours of our country.  
The second point I want to make is, as the custodia n of the well-being of the farmers' 
interests, I would like to congratulate our Ministe r also. This year, thanks again to our 
capability in meteorology and space science, the ea rly forecast shows that the coming 
south-west monsoon may be a regular one. We hope, it will be a regular one. But, what is the 
purpose of the forecast? To be forewarned is forearmed; if you know that you are going to 
have a fairly regular monsoon; that it is time we prepare what I call a good weather code and 
plan how to optimise the benefits of good rainfall and, of course, we must also be prepared 
to minimise the impact of adverse monsoon. Nationally, this coming agricultural year starting 
in June, in the year 2008-09, we require accelerate d agricultural progress. There is an 
opportunity, there is a national compulsion. There is also an international compulsion 
because all indications are that the world food prices are not going to go down; in fact, they 
may go up if China and India go in a large scale to the international market. Therefore, this 
unique year 2008-09 is a sort of a watershed year i n our country and we must make the 
maximum use.  
What do I mean by a good weather code? It means how do you maximise the benefits of 
a good weather by attending to all the links with which I started, starting with the soil, soil 
healthcare, water harvesting and water management, credit and insurance, technology and 
inputs, and, above all, pricing and marketing. One thing we should take care, over 60 per 
cent of our area is rain-fed. Therefore, these are areas which will benefit most from a good 
monsoon. What are the crops of these areas — millet , jowar, bajra, and also a large number 
of pulses, oilseeds, and so on. We have allowed a zero import duty on many of these crops 
like pulses and oilseeds. What I will request the h on. Agriculture Minister is to watch the 
market because many times the imports come just at times when our harvests are there. And 
these are very poor people. Although Support Prices  are announced for a large number of 
crops, it is only in wheat and rice that it is really operational. In all other cases, when you go
